theme: Taller, shorter, longer, heavier, and how many blocks tall

activities.title: Which one is taller
activities.intro: Two things at a time. Listen for the word, then tap the one it fits.
activities.offScreen: Stand two spoons up on the table, one tall one and one little one, and ask them to hand you the taller one.

rounds.prompt: Two blocks, one big and one little. Tap the taller block.
Two flowers. Tap the shorter flower.
Two fish. Tap the longer fish.
Two rocks. The bigger rock is the heavier one. Tap the heavier rock.

activities.title: How many blocks tall
activities.intro: Something stands beside a pile of blocks that reaches exactly as far as it does. It is only there to look at. Count the blocks, then tap how many.
activities.offScreen: Lie a spoon on the floor and lay blocks along it, end to end, until they reach, then count them out loud together.

rounds.prompt: The flower is as tall as this pile of blocks. The flower is just standing there. Count only the blocks, and tap how many.
The fish is as long as this pile of blocks. The fish is just swimming there. Count only the blocks, and tap how many.
The rock is as tall as this pile of blocks. The rock is just sitting there. Count only the blocks, and tap how many.
The leaf is as long as this pile of blocks. The leaf is just lying there. Count only the blocks, and tap how many.

activities.title: Towers with the same number of blocks
activities.intro: A grey tower lies beside three coloured ones. Count the blocks in the grey tower, then tap the coloured tower with exactly the same number of blocks.
activities.offScreen: Build a tower of four blocks, then ask them to build one just as tall next to it without knocking yours over.

rounds.prompt: Count the blocks in the grey tower. Now tap the coloured tower with exactly the same number of blocks.
Count the blocks in the grey tower. Now tap the coloured tower with exactly the same number of blocks.
Count the blocks in the grey tower. Now tap the coloured tower with exactly the same number of blocks.
The grey tower is a little one. Count its blocks, then tap the coloured tower with exactly the same number of blocks.

parentCard.title: Measure the family in blocks
steps: Lie them down on the floor and lay blocks end to end from the top of their head to their heels. Count them together, one number for one block, and say the number twice.
Do the same for one more person in the family. Leave both lines of blocks lying on the floor, side by side, so both can be seen at once.
Ask who is taller and let them point before anybody says a number. If they point at the shorter line, do not correct it, just count both lines again together and ask again.
Ask how many more blocks the taller one needed, and count the extra blocks with them, touching each one.
Let them choose the last thing to measure, even if it is the cat, and let them say the number at the end.
notice: Do they count one number for one block, without skipping a block or counting one twice?
Do they use taller and longer for the right things, or is everything just big?
With the two lines of blocks side by side, do they compare them by looking, or do they need to count both first?
